elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable and other work product created for Customer". "Deliverable" (1.4) captures reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials created specifically for Customer, and the added "other work product created for Customer" language extends beyond the Order-Form-identified definition.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable and work product" — a present-tense operative assignment, not a promise to assign.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.3 (unchanged): "Vendor retains Vendor Technology." Vendor Technology is defined at 1.8 as Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines and connectors, and 1.4 expressly excludes Vendor Technology from Deliverables, so the new 14.2 assignment does not swallow Vendor's pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 13.2 grants a "perpetual ... licence" for "software and Vendor Technology ... embedded in a Deliverable", and 14.3 routes incorporated or necessary Vendor Technology to that Section 13.2 licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" applying to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable; 14.3 cross-refers to it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer." No assignment of Customer Data to Vendor survives.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.4: "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights" — joint ownership only by later signed instrument that must specify exploitation rights, so no unrestricted-exploitation gap arises by default.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; 1.4 excludes from Deliverables "Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel", so the new 14.2 assignment does not reach generic tools or know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Condition effectively inapplicable: under revised 14.2 Customer owns the Deliverables outright and Vendor assigns all right, title and interest, so no licence to Deliverables is needed; ownership is a superset of a perpetual licence. The former revocable, Order-Form-term licence in 14.2 has been deleted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Inapplicable by operation: Customer holds title to the Deliverables under revised 14.2, so there is no revocable Vendor grant; the prior "revocable, non-transferable licence" language is removed.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Inapplicable by operation: outright ownership under revised 14.2 is unrestricted as to territory; embedded Vendor Technology is separately licensed "worldwide" under 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Inapplicable by operation: the assignment in 14.2 carries no royalty obligation, and 13.2 covers embedded Vendor material on a "royalty-free, fully paid" basis.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership under revised 14.2 confers unrestricted use and modification rights; 13.2 separately permits Customer to "modify, create derivative works from" embedded Vendor Technology, so no residual restriction blocks modification.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Inapplicable by operation: as owner of the Deliverables Customer may license or transfer them; the prior "non-transferable" restriction in 14.2 has been struck. Embedded Vendor Technology remains governed by 13.2 (Affiliates and supporting contractors), a carve-out consistent with Vendor retaining its pre-existing IP.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: original 14.2 gave Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables created for Customer with only a "revocable, non-transferable licence ... during the applicable Order Form term", which fails the fallback (revocable, term-limited, non-sublicensable) as well as the preferred position. The 13.2 perpetual licence does not cure this because it reaches only software/Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself.

Preferred level is complete. The single edit to 14.2 supplies both open elements (Customer ownership plus a present-tense Vendor assignment), and the remaining six preferred elements are already met in unmodified operative text (14.1 Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.3 Vendor Technology retention and cross-reference; 13.2 perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence; 14.4 no joint ownership).

The fallback checklist is also satisfied a fortiori: ownership plus assignment subsumes a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense, and 1.4/1.8 plus 14.3 leave Vendor's generic tools and know-how untouched.

Minimal: only the one non-compliant sentence pair in 14.2 was rewritten. No duplicate licence grant was inserted alongside the assignment, 13.2/14.1/14.3/14.4 were left intact, and no extra requirements (e.g. escrow, source code, moral-rights waiver, IP indemnity uplift) were added beyond the checklist.

Preserves intent: Vendor still owns its platform and Vendor Technology, the pre-delivery identification duty and third-party-material approval right in 14.3 survive, the feedback mechanic in 14.4 is unchanged, and Order Form fee/term mechanics are unaffected. No internal contradiction remains because the revocable term-limited licence it replaced was deleted rather than left standing.

Drafting note only, not a defect: the revised 14.2 assigns "all right, title, and interest" without an express "including all intellectual property rights therein" or a moral-rights waiver, and does not spell out that the assignment is subject to Vendor's retained Vendor Technology. The latter is nonetheless resolved by 1.4's exclusion of Vendor Technology from Deliverables and by 14.3, so no checklist element is unmet; if Vendor pushes back, adding "subject to Section 14.3" would be a costless clarification.
The margin comment accurately describes the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback licence if Vendor insists on retaining title; tone is concise and first person plural.
